correct_completion: she submitted it to the committee.
full_sentence: Having finished the report, she submitted it to the committee.
acceptable_variants: she then handed it to the committee.
she gave the committee the finished version.

options.why_wrong: The participle phrase 'Having finished' must describe the subject of the main clause; here the committee would be the one who finished the report, which is illogical.
A second participle appears with no finite main clause, so the sentence is incomplete.

options.text: she submitted it to the committee.
it was submitted to the committee.
options.why_wrong: The subject 'it' (the report) cannot logically be the one who finished the report, so the participle clause dangles.

grammar_focus: Perfect participle clause ('Having + past participle') with the same subject as the main clause
explanation: A perfect participle clause must refer to the same subject as the main clause, so the person who finished the report must be the one who submitted it.
